children: a project agreement with the Nyangumarta Warrarn aboriginal group to secure a long-term partnership for the development of the Winu copper-and-gold mine in Australia, clearing a key hurdle for the company as it targets first production by 2030.
Winu, located in Western Australia's Great Sandy Desert, is Rio Tinto's
most advanced near-term greenfield copper project and an important part of the company's strategy to grow its copper portfolio.

Through the agreement, Nyangumarta people gave consent for the proposed Winu mine and associated infrastructure on Nyangumarta Country, although the project remains subject to regulatory and other required approvals, as well as a final investment decision.
The deal builds on a project planning pact signed in 2023 and establishes how the Nyangumarta people and Rio
will work together as planning progresses, including measures to avoid impacts on the environment and aboriginal cultural heritage.

title: Rio Tinto secures aboriginal consent for Winu copper project in Australia
